mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, I just want to say—if you’re still listening, you’ve already taken a brave and meaningful step. Facing the truth of your story takes so much honesty and courage. Healing from the wounds of a narcissistic mother isn’t a simple, straight path. And you know what? You don’t have to do it alone. This journey isn’t just about understanding your past. It’s about reclaiming your present and shaping the kind of future you truly deserve. So here are a few reminders to keep close as you move forward: Your feelings and needs—they’re real. They matter, even if no one ever acknowledged them before. Setting boundaries? That’s not selfish. It’s an act of self-respect. Healing is a process, not a one-time event. There’ll be ups and downs, and that’s okay. Remember, you’re not responsible for your mom’s happiness or her emotional balance. And real connection is possible—with yourself, and with people who truly see and value you. The patterns you learned growing up? Those were survival tactics, not signs of weakness. It’s perfectly natural to grieve, to feel anger or sadness, and to hold hope for something better. Every little act of self-care, every honest conversation, every boundary you set—it’s all a step toward your own freedom. You’re definitely not alone on this road. There are others walking right alongside you, and there’s support out there—through therapy, through community, or even just by sharing your story. The work may be tough, but the rewards are real: more peace, more confidence, and relationships that truly nurture you. Above all, please remember—you're worthy of love, respect, and joy. Not because of what you do, but simply because of who you are. So now, the question isn’t, “Will I ever be good enough?” It’s, “How can I honor the person I’m becoming?” Trust yourself. You’ve got the strength to answer that, one day at a time.
